segments.text: A mosquito lands on Gummy's arm.
The spot gets itchy right away.
But mosquitoes aren't what's making it itch.
Mosquitoes inject saliva that keeps blood from clotting.
His body spots it as an outside invader.
It fires back with a defense chemical.
That chemical widens blood vessels and sets off nerves.
That's why the bite swells up and itches.
Scratching spreads it - and can make it itch even more.
